name: Kanazawa Umimirai Library
key_features: Concrete skin punctured by some 6,000 small circular glass blocks in a triangular array.

name: Waseda International House of Literature (Haruki Murakami Library)
key_features: Rebuilt from the old Building 4; shelves over 3,000 Murakami books in more than 50 languages.

name: Okinawa Prefecture Government Building
key_features: Fourteen floors above ground and two below, opened in 1990; one of Naha's tallest buildings.

name: Yufuin Station
key_features: Station building inspired by a chapel, designed by Arata Isozaki and completed in 1990.

name: Hibiya Public Hall
key_features: Japan's first full-scale concert hall and an early steel-frame reinforced concrete building; won a design competition.

name: Sacred Heart Cathedral (Yamate Catholic Church), Yokohama
key_features: Rebuilt Neo-Gothic cathedral designed by the Czech architect Jan Josef Svagr and completed in 1933.

name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral
key_features: Romanesque Revival cathedral with mosaic murals; construction began in 1922 to Arthur Dixon's design.

name: Guangzhou Library
key_features: Stacked, cascading 'book' forms on the facade; the design concept is 'Beautiful Books'.

name: Wuhan Railway Station
by: AREP, Fourth Survey and Design Institute of China, MaP3, SNCF-IGOA
key_features: Nine separate parts stand for China's nine provinces; the roof takes its form from the yellow crane, Wuhan's symbol.

name: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre
key_features: Glass curtain wall, the world's largest when built, looking over Victoria Harbour on three sides.

name: Hong Kong Central Library
key_features: Plan built from three shapes: the circle for sky, the square for land, the triangle for accumulated knowledge.

name: Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre
key_features: Daniel Libeskind's building for City University of Hong Kong's creative media school, designed with Leigh & Orange.

name: New Beijing Poly Plaza
key_features: Glass cable-net wall, called the world's largest; the lantern atrium has no support columns at the ground.

name: HSBC Building, the Bund
key_features: Main trading hall has columns made from whole marble blocks, unusual in Asia at the time.

name: Rockbund Art Museum
key_features: Chipperfield's restoration kept the original 1932 street facade and a minimalist approach.

name: Hainan Science and Technology Museum
key_features: Spiral form around a large open core, clad in 843 fibre-reinforced polymer panels.

name: Red House Theater
key_features: Western and Meiji-era Japanese patterns blended; an octagonal section joins a cruciform building and a square.

name: Shenzhen Cultural Center (Library and Concert Hall)
key_features: Concert hall with vineyard-style seating for 1,800, beside the Shenzhen Library; both by Arata Isozaki.

name: Mercedes-Benz Arena (Expo Culture Center)
key_features: Nicknamed 'the Clam Shell' and 'the Hamburger'; the arena seats 18,000.

name: Olympic Park Observation Tower
by: Cui Kai, Li Cundong, Zhao Wenbin (China Architecture Design & Research Group)
key_features: Inspired by blades of grass; its five circular tops echo the Olympic rings.

name: Shanghai Library East
key_features: Open plan that gives most space to the community; its form refers abstractly to Taihu stones.

name: National Theater and Concert Hall
by: Yang Cho-cheng, Architects and Engineers Associates
key_features: Modern in function but recalling traditional Chinese palace architecture; stands at Liberty Square.

name: Sullivan Center (Carson Pirie Scott Building)
key_features: Chicago School store of 1899–1907: ornate cast-iron base, white terracotta grid above, 12 stories.

name: Willis Tower (Sears Tower)
by: Bruce Graham, Fazlur Khan (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill)
key_features: 110 stories, 442 m, built as nine square tubes in a 3×3 bundle; black aluminium and glass facade.

name: Peter B. Lewis Building (Weatherhead School of Management)
key_features: Gehry's 2002 business school: about 150,000 sq ft over five stories, offices and classrooms mixed on every floor.

name: Minneapolis Central Library
key_features: César Pelli's 2006 library of 353,000 sq ft with an atrium and an 18,560 sq ft green roof.

name: Kemper Arena (Hy-Vee Arena)
key_features: Arena of 1974 whose roof hangs from exterior steel trusses on three portals, leaving no interior columns.

name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
key_features: Semicircular fountain about 64 ft tall, matching the tower's 64 stories, set among 118 live oaks.

name: Hall of State, Fair Park
key_features: Art Deco exhibition hall with a curved exedra entrance flanked by 76 ft limestone pillars.

name: Nasher Museum of Art
key_features: Duke University's art museum, designed by Rafael Viñoly and completed in 2005 in a Modern style.

name: Schermerhorn Symphony Center
by: David M. Schwarz Architects with Earl Swensson Associates
key_features: New Classical concert hall: shoebox auditorium with 30 clerestory windows and a 3,568-pipe Schoenstein organ.

name: Memphis Pyramid
key_features: 321-ft pyramid arena playing on Memphis, Egypt; now a Bass Pro Shops store with a lookout at the apex.

name: Florida State Capitol
by: Edward Durell Stone & Associates with Reynolds, Smith & Hills
key_features: Concrete New Formalist tower of 22 floors and 345 ft, its windows shaded by metal louvers.

name: Reynolds Building
key_features: 21-storey, 314-ft Art Deco tower, a design inspiration for the Empire State Building; marble interiors.

name: First Baptist Church, Columbus
key_features: Red brick in five sections around a central courtyard; a windowless sanctuary under a steep gable.

name: Fire Station No. 4, Columbus
by: Robert Venturi and Denise Scott Brown (Venturi and Rauch)
key_features: Trapezoid plan; a semicircular entrance tower topped with a large yellow number 4.

name: First Unitarian Society Meeting House
key_features: Prow-like blue-green copper roof over hinged-arch trusses; 64 ft interior span; limestone walls hauled by members.

name: UTS Tower (UTS Building 1)
key_features: Landmark 27-floor brutalist tower on Broadway, finished 1979 from a 1968 plan.

name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
key_features: Steel through-arch bridge for rail, road, bicycles and walkers, designed and built by Dorman Long.

name: Public Transport Centre (former Westrail Centre)
key_features: Brutalist terminal and administration building of East Perth Terminal, opened 12 November 1976.

name: Telstra Tower (Black Mountain Tower)
by: Richard Ure and the Commonwealth Department of Works
key_features: 195.2 m tower above Black Mountain, the tallest structure in Canberra, with indoor and outdoor viewing platforms.

name: Puaka-James Hight Building
key_features: 53 m brutalist library tower of exposed concrete, the University of Canterbury's best-known building.

name: Manchester Unity Building
key_features: Art Deco Gothic-inspired office tower built 1931-32 opposite Melbourne Town Hall.

name: Paganin House
key_features: Floreat house of 1965, an icon of mid-century modern architecture in Australia.

name: Hyde Park Barracks
key_features: Convict-built barracks of 1811 to 1819, now a museum and part of the Australian Convict Sites.

name: National Wine Centre of Australia
key_features: Opened 6 October 2001 beside the Adelaide Botanic Garden, designed by Philip Cox.

name: Jubilee Library
key_features: Among England's most energy-efficient public buildings: half the carbon footprint of a traditional equivalent.

name: River & Rowing Museum
key_features: Chipperfield museum by the Thames; Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year, 1999.

name: Kirklees Stadium (John Smith's Stadium)
key_features: Stadium built in stages from 1994; RIBA Building of the Year for 1995.

name: Kuggen
key_features: Round tower in glazed terracotta in six reds and two greens, with a sun-tracking solar screen.

name: Whitechapel Gallery
key_features: Early British Modern Style building; one of London's first public galleries for temporary shows.

name: mumok
key_features: Cubic museum clad in basalt lava stone in the MuseumsQuartier.

name: Zwinger
key_features: Richly decorated Baroque pavilions linked by galleries lined with balustrades, figures and vases.

name: Würzburg Residence
key_features: Baroque palace whose interiors include a grand staircase, a chapel and the Imperial Hall.

name: Siemensstadt Estate (Ringsiedlung)
by: Hans Scharoun (master plan) with Fred Forbát, Otto Bartning, Walter Gropius, Hugo Häring and Paul Rudolf Henning
key_features: UNESCO-listed modernist housing estate of 1929–31, planned by Hans Scharoun with five other architects.

name: Karlskirche
by: Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach (completed by Joseph Emanuel Fischer von Erlach)
key_features: Baroque church with a dome over a high drum, a Greek-temple portico and two flanking columns inspired by Trajan's.

name: Wieskirche
key_features: Oval Rococo church with a semi-circular narthex, stucco decoration and trompe-l'oeil ceilings.

name: Sprinkenhof
by: Fritz Höger, Hans Gerson and Oskar Gerson
key_features: Brick Expressionism on a reinforced-concrete skeleton; rhombic clinker patterns decorate the facade.

name: Yenidze
key_features: Former cigarette factory in Moorish Revival style, borrowing from mosques and the Alhambra as advertising.

name: Universum Bremen
key_features: Clad in 40,000 stainless steel scales, the building resembles a mixture of a whale and a mussel.

name: Sammlung Goetz
key_features: Purpose-built museum for a private contemporary art collection, with video and film shown on the lower level.

name: St. Jakob-Park
key_features: Switzerland's largest football stadium with 32 shops on three floors inside; seats about 37,500.

name: Hangar-7
key_features: Airfoil-shaped steel-and-glass dome: 1,200 tons of steel and 75,000 sq ft of glass.

name: Vitra Conference Pavilion
key_features: Tadao Ando's first building outside Japan; gridded concrete and holes for light define its style.

name: Walter-Gropius-Haus (Interbau)
by: Walter Gropius / The Architects' Collaborative with Wils Ebert
key_features: Nine-floor concrete-skeleton block of 66 apartments built for the 1957 Interbau exhibition.

name: University Library Freiburg
key_features: 7,300 m² facade of glass and matted dark chrome steel; reading rooms along the south side of each floor.

name: Neues Museum Nürnberg
key_features: Museum of modern art and design in Nuremberg's old town; construction ran from 1996 to October 1999.

name: Mossehaus
key_features: Mendelsohn's 1921–23 corner rebuild: strips and sculpted elements in the fenestration gave a dynamic form.

name: Olympiastadion
key_features: Built 1934–36; the field is sunk 2.65 m and the western end opens to reveal the Bell Tower.

name: Neue Wache
key_features: Prussian Neoclassical guardhouse with a Doric portico; today a memorial lit by an oculus.

name: Rheinturm
key_features: Concrete telecommunications tower with a revolving restaurant and Horst Baumann's light-sculpture clock on the shaft.

name: Esbjerg Performing Arts Centre
key_features: Concert hall designed by Jan Utzon with his father Jørn Utzon, beside the Art Museum in the City Park.

name: Korshagehus
key_features: Modernist summer house the architect built for himself; garage and guesthouse added 1965 and 1984.

name: Röhsska Museum
key_features: National Romantic design museum building, opened to the public in 1916.

name: Wenner-Gren Center
key_features: Three buildings, Helicon, Pylon and Tetragon: a high tower with a lower semicircular building around it.

name: Landskrona City Hall
key_features: Modernist city hall by the new harbour, inaugurated in September 1976.

name: Lillehammer Art Museum
key_features: Snøhetta's wing, opened 1992, joins an older building by Erling Viksjø.

name: Stavanger Konserthus
key_features: Concert hall with an orchestra hall and a multi-purpose hall, opened 15 September 2012.

name: Kunstnernes Hus
key_features: Artists' House, a prominent Functionalist building, opened on 1 October 1930.

name: Museum of Central Finland
key_features: Cultural history museum in a building designed by Alvar Aalto, completed in 1960.

name: Sähkötalo
key_features: Headquarters of the city energy company, built from March 1970 to January 1973.

name: Ympyrätalo
key_features: Circle-shaped building in Hakaniemi, opened 1968 and renovated 2002–2004.

name: Seinäjoki Library
key_features: Library completed in 1965 as part of Aalto's centre; the new Apila library (JKMM, 2012) stands beside it.

name: Finnish National Theatre
key_features: National Romantic theatre of 1902 beside Helsinki Central Station square.

name: Uspenski Cathedral
key_features: Orthodox cathedral in Russian Revival style, built 1862–1868 under Ivan Varnek.

name: Tampere Hall
key_features: Largest congress centre in the Nordic countries, inaugurated 29 September 1990.

name: Muurame church
key_features: One of Aalto's early works, completed in 1929.

name: Seinäjoki Civil Guard House
key_features: One of Aalto's first public buildings, designed 1924–1926 in Nordic Classicism.

name: Espoo Cultural Centre
key_features: Culture centre in Tapiola that holds the central library, completed in 1989.

name: National Theatre of Iceland
key_features: National theatre, formally opened on 20 April 1950.

name: Westminster Cathedral
key_features: Neo-Byzantine brick cathedral built without steel reinforcement; John Betjeman called it a masterpiece in striped brick and stone.

name: Flatiron Building
key_features: A 22-storey steel-framed tower filling a triangular block where Fifth Avenue meets Broadway.

name: Yodokō Guest House
key_features: Wright's only surviving residence in Japan, four levels stepped into a hill overlooking Osaka Bay.

name: Pettit Memorial Chapel
key_features: Wright's only funerary structure built in his lifetime, a Prairie Style chapel in Belvidere Cemetery.

name: Itatiaia Building
key_features: Campinas's first Modernist building, by Oscar Niemeyer, often compared with Copan in São Paulo.

name: One Charles Center
key_features: Mies van der Rohe's aluminium and glass International Style tower, the first modernist office tower in Baltimore.

name: Złota 44
key_features: Libeskind's 52-story residential tower in central Warsaw, inspired by an eagle's wing and called Żagiel.

name: Saint-Denis–Pleyel station
key_features: Kengo Kuma's station, opened June 2024 as the terminus of Paris Metro Line 14 on the Grand Paris Express.

name: Torre Realia BCN
key_features: Toyo Ito's 24-floor, 112-metre tower on Plaça d'Europa, L'Hospitalet, completed in 2009.

name: Onomichi City Museum of Art
key_features: Tadao Ando's 2003 redesign of Onomichi's art museum in Senkō-ji Park, first opened in 1980.
